sections.h2: What should a Coral Gables seller know before choosing how to sell?
sections.html:
A Coral Gables house can sell three ways: through an agent listing, as a for-sale-by-owner deal, or to a cash buyer who takes the property as it stands. The right route depends on the house's age, its condition, and how soon you need the money.

The city calls itself the "City Beautiful," and the city's own site says more than 1,000 properties sit on the Coral Gables Register of Historic Places. If your home is one of them, ask the city before you plan renovations, because a historic designation can shape what a buyer is allowed to change. Census lists the median gross rent at $2,373, so some owners also weigh keeping the house as a rental against selling it.

sections.h2: How big is Coral Gables and who lives there?
sections.html:
Coral Gables is a Miami-Dade County city of 49,578 people as of the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, spread over 12.93 square miles of land. That works out to a density of 3,809.7 people per square mile in 2020.

The housing numbers below come from Census QuickFacts and show a high-value market with a lot of older stock.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for a Coral Gables home sale?
sections.html:
Employers and institutions support a steady pool of buyers who relocate for work. The city lists more than 20 consulates and foreign government offices and more than 140 multinational corporations within its limits.

  • Census counts 2022 retail sales of $2,590,246 thousand and health care and social assistance receipts of $2,305,822 thousand in the city.
  • The mean commute for workers is 23.8 minutes, shorter than the 26.4 minute U.S. figure on the same page.
  • Census puts 73.6% of adults 25 and older at a bachelor's degree or higher.

Buyers from outside the area often want a clean title file and quick closing, so sellers who have paperwork ready tend to avoid delays.

sections.h2: What permits and city rules affect selling in Coral Gables?
sections.html:
Start with the city's permits page, which lists every permit the city issues, and its City Services Directory for anything you cannot find. Open or expired permits on a house are a common reason a closing stalls, so ask the building staff whether any permit on your address is still open.

Large development and traffic calming projects are listed on the city's Development and City Projects page, which is worth a look if a project sits near your street. Meeting agendas and public notices are posted under City Meetings.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when a Coral Gables house is sold?
sections.html:
Florida charges documentary stamp tax on the deed, and Miami-Dade County has its own schedule. The Department of Revenue prints 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax for Miami-Dade, with the surtax not due on a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling. The Department of Revenue states that every party to the document is liable regardless of who agrees to pay; the base rate is set in s. 201.02.

  • The clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded.
  • Recording charges are set in s. 28.24: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus trust fund and technology charges.
  • A deed must be in writing and signed before two witnesses under s. 689.01.

Ask the title company for the final settlement figures before signing.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when a Coral Gables home sells?
sections.html:
Florida assesses property each January 1, and a sale resets the assessed value to just value the next year. That is why a buyer's bill can be far higher than the seller's, particularly on a homestead that has been capped for many years under Save Our Homes.

  • The Save Our Homes cap limits yearly growth to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change.
  • The homestead exemption is up to $50,000, applied for by March 1 with the property appraiser.
  • Homestead is lost if the house is rented out or stops being your permanent home.

The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser says its office does not send tax bills. The county tax collector bills and collects, with an early-payment discount that runs from 4 percent in November down to 1 percent in February. The appraiser certified the 2026 tax roll on October 16, 2026. For questions about your assessment, call the appraiser's public service line at 305-375-4712.

sections.h2: What if the house has a mortgage default, a tenant or an estate?
sections.html:
Each situation has its own clock. A foreclosure sale happens 20 to 35 days after final judgment, and a homeowner should ask the clerk about surplus funds within 10 days of the sale. A deed from a personal representative under a probated will is not taxable for doc stamps.

  • Estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt property may use summary administration under s. 735.201.
  • A tenant on a month-to-month lease needs 30 days' notice to end the tenancy under s. 83.57.
  • Nonpayment of rent starts with a 3 day written notice.

Miami-Dade also offers free fraud alerts through the Clerk of Court, which warn you within 24 hours when a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name. Signing up is sensible for anyone who owns a vacant or inherited home.

sections.h2: What steps does a Coral Gables sale follow after you accept an offer?
sections.html:
The deed has to be written, signed in front of two witnesses, and recorded with the Miami-Dade clerk. Florida permits the witnessing to happen by audio-video technology, so an owner who has moved away can still sign.

  • Gather mortgage payoff information and any open permit records.
  • Confirm whether your homestead exemption will end with the sale, since the new owner starts at full assessed value.
  • Ask the title agent how the January 1 assessment date and the November tax bill will be split between you and the buyer.
  • Keep a copy of the recorded deed.

Owners who plan to buy another Florida home should file the portability form with the new homestead application so the old cap carries over, up to the limit printed in Save Our Homes guidance.

faqs.q: How much is a typical Coral Gables house worth?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts lists a median value of $1,089,900 for owner-occupied housing units in Coral Gables for 2020-2024. Your own house may be far above or below that figure depending on size, lot and condition.

faqs.q: Does a historic designation affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can. The city says more than 1,000 properties are on its Register of Historic Places, and a buyer should know about any rules before closing. Ask the city staff about your address.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a Coral Gables deed?
faqs.a: Every party to the deed is liable under Florida law, no matter who agrees to pay. The clerk collects it at recording, and Miami-Dade uses 60 cents per $100 with a surtax that does not apply to a document transferring only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: Will my property taxes follow me to a new home?
faqs.a: They can partly. Florida portability lets you carry over homestead savings if you set up a new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, filed with Form DR-501T by March 1.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about my assessment?
faqs.a: Ask the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser. Its public service line is 305-375-4712, and the office also runs a branch at the South Dade Government Center in Cutler Bay.
